integrator_questions: With wheel_radius at 0.025 m, does the controller need more kp to hold the bend response, or can kd be relaxed? Compare the gain margin with the 0.030 m and 0.035 m runs.
Where does max_error occur now: on the oval's tightest bend, or on the s-bend and slalom? If the peak is still at bend entry, wheel geometry alone will not close the gap.
Does steering_oscillation or control_effort fall with the smaller wheels, and does oval progress drop more than the s-bend and slalom gain?

intent: Single-variable test of wheel_radius on the best design (iteration 7, 73.33). Wheel radius goes from 0.030 m to 0.025 m, reversing the 0.035 m step that scored 64.78. Everything else matches iteration 7: 80 mm sensor row, 12 mm sensors on a 12 mm pitch, 0.12 m track, 1.0 kg, 0.12 m body width, 0.18 m body length. Expected: s-bend and slalom progress rise above the iteration 7 values, oval progress falls slightly, max_error moves toward 0.060 m, and the score beats 73.33.
learning: Lookahead, track and mass are now at measured optima (80 mm, 0.12 m, about 1.0 kg). The wheel-radius result (0.035 m scored 64.78, below 0.030 m at 73.33) shows that larger wheels hurt bend performance even though they raise oval progress. The next test checks the other side: if 0.025 m beats 0.030 m, the optimum radius is below 0.030 m and the next step is 0.022 m or a sensor-size change. If 0.025 m falls back, 0.030 m is the local optimum and sensor size (16 mm) is the next single-variable test.
rationale: Scores so far: the best design is iteration 7 (80 mm sensor row, 12 mm sensors on a 12 mm pitch, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 1.0 kg) at 73.33. Lookahead (40 to 80 mm), track (0.10 to 0.14 m) and mass (0.6 to 1.2 kg) have each been tested in isolation and each shows a peak or a monotone optimum near the current values. Iteration 9 raised wheel_radius from 0.030 to 0.035 m and scored 64.78, a 8.6-point drop. Oval progress rose (0.227 to 0.273), but s-bend (0.194 to 0.078 progress in the authorised per-track data) and slalom fell. Every run still ends off track with max_error at 0.060 to 0.066 m, just over the 0.06 m limit, while rms_error stays at 0.02 to 0.03 m, so the failure is a transient bend peak rather than a steady offset. The wheel-radius result is consistent with the earlier track results: the radius-to-track ratio (0.25 at baseline, 0.29 at iteration 9) appears to govern bend response. Larger wheels make the robot faster on the straight but less able to correct on tight bends. I therefore reverse the direction: wheel_radius goes from 0.030 to 0.025 m (ratio about 0.21), holding every other value at the iteration 7 baseline. Expected result: s-bend and slalom progress recover and max_error moves toward or below 0.06 m, at some cost to oval speed. The score should land above 73.33 if the ratio hypothesis holds. If it falls again, the ratio is not the main lever, and the next single-variable test is sensor size (16 mm) at the baseline radius.
